audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 read 'Skill' while its own content why says the sustained trade still favours her, and the 2+ item row read Riven while its why calls the late duel parity.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Riven / Riven / Riven / Skill / Riven / Skill, and the mirror riven__sylas already flipped those same two rows. Riven owns everything from level 2 to her first item; Sylas gets back to level only at two items.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 to Riven and 2+ items to Skill in matched phases[].side + win[] pairs, with both why lines rewritten to match their new sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] describes the level 6 steal as 'mostly neutral — she keeps her empowered Q and W from it anyway', which is muddled, and never says why the steal is weak.
audit.why: Blade of the Exile grants attack damage and attack range plus one Wind Slash. Sylas builds ability power, so this is one of the least valuable ultimates in the game for him to hold — that is the actual reason level 6 does not flip this lane, and the page never says it.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and whys[4] rewritten to state the AD-versus-AP mismatch plainly, leaving Kingslayer as the real level 6 tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields tell the player to land the E hook 'to stun' Riven — whys[0], early, mid, wants.you[0] and the trade lines.
audit.why: Abscond's recast (Abduct) throws chains and pulls Sylas to the enemy he hits; there is no stun and the kit carries no hardCC flag on E. The mirror flagged the same claim and declined to assert it. It matters more here than anywhere: the whole plan was 'hook her before Ki Burst', and if the hook does not stun, the pull actually delivers Sylas into a 260-range stun he was trying to pre-empt.
audit.corrected: Stun claims replaced with the chain pull, and the advice re-keyed to Ki Burst's 11/10/9/8/7s cooldown and Valor's 10-6s shield-dash instead of to phantom CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d says a whiffed Ki Burst gives you the lane 'briefly' with no number, and Broken Wings' cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: Ki Burst is 11/10/9/8/7s and Broken Wings is a flat 13s for the whole three-cast chain — the two numbers that tell a Sylas when he is allowed to exist. Neither was on the page.
audit.corrected: Ki Burst's window written into dosFull[2].d, Broken Wings' 13s into phases[3].why.

edits.before: Weave passive autos between every spell. Trade around Ki Burst (Stun) and bank small HP leads — they compound at 6.
edits.after: Broken Wings is a 13s chain she cancels into autos and Valor shields your answer — she picks the trade, you react.

edits.before: Two items plus a stolen ult makes you a teamfight flex — flank, burst the carry, and steal the scariest R on cooldown.
edits.after: Two items brings your sustain back to parity, but Blade of the Exile pays in attack damage and does nothing for you.

edits.before: Riven whiffs Ki Burst (Stun) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Riven whiffs Ki Burst — that is 7-11 seconds of open lane.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — Abduct only pulls you in, and a melee mage has no exit without it.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Abduct does not stun — it drops you inside Ki Burst's 260 range with your escape already spent.

edits.before: Level 1 you only have Q chain lash or W — no E hook, no stun — so neither of you can force a real all-in, but Riven's single Q dash keeps you honest at farm range.
edits.after: Level 1 you have Chain Lash or Kingslayer and no Abscond, so neither of you can force a real all-in — but Riven's first Broken Wings dash keeps you honest at farm range.

edits.before: At level 6 you steal Blade of the Exile but it scales on AP you do not fully have yet — your W heal keeps you in the fight, making this a true skill window where landing E hook first is the decisive factor.
edits.after: At level 6 you steal Blade of the Exile, but it pays in attack damage and range that an AP Sylas cannot spend — the W heal is what keeps you level, so the window turns on who commits first.

edits.before: Stealing Riven's Blade of the Exile with your R is mostly neutral — she keeps her empowered Q and W from it anyway, but at 6 your W heal keeps you alive through her burst window if you can land your E hook.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile is among the worst ultimates you can hold — it grants attack damage and range, which an AP build cannot spend, so at six your real tool is still the Kingslayer heal and her spent Ki Burst.

edits.before: Land E hook first to stun Riven before she can W-stun you and open her full Q-dash combo
edits.after: Chain in before Ki Burst lands — Abduct pulls you to her and does not stun, so move first

edits.before: W-stun you at the start of every trade so your E hook is wasted or unused and she gets a free combo rotation
edits.after: Open every trade with Ki Burst — a 7-11s stun on demand, and your chain has no CC to answer it

edits.before: At level 1 neither of you has a meaningful engage pattern — Riven has one Q dash but no stun or shield yet, and you only have Q chain lash or W without your E hook. Farm safely with Q chain lash at the edge of its range and do not step into her Q dash range. The real danger begins the moment she hits level 2: her Q-into-W-stun sequence arrives before you can react if you are standing close, so always be ready to E-hook her pre-emptively the instant she starts a Q dash toward you, stunning her before her W can lock you down. Levels 1-2 belong to Riven because she gets her full short-trade kit before you get your hook — respect that window and do not contest it without E available.
edits.after: At level 1 neither of you has a meaningful engage pattern — Riven has one Q dash but no stun or shield yet, and you only have Chain Lash or Kingslayer without Abscond. Farm safely at the edge of Chain Lash range and do not step into her Broken Wings range. The real danger begins the moment she hits level 2: her Q-into-Ki-Burst sequence lands before you can react if you are standing close, and Abduct will not stop it because the recast only pulls you to her. Use Abscond to leave, not to meet her. Levels 1-2 belong to Riven because she completes her short-trade kit before you complete yours — respect that window and do not contest it without E available.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 are still Riven's strongest window: her Q-Q-Q animation-cancelled combo with W-stun in the middle and E-shield absorbing your Q burst means every extended trade has her dealing physical damage while your W heal tries to compensate. The trade pattern you want is: bait her E shield first by poking with Q chain lash, then once Valor is on cooldown E-hook her to stun, immediately W Kingslayer for the missing-health damage and healing, and use your Passive chain autos between casts. Do not let her E out cleanly before your W lands — if she shields your Q and then dashes away, you healed nothing and she won. At level 6 the lane resets to a genuine skill matchup: stealing Blade of the Exile gives you her empowered Q and W, but you are using AP scaling on her AD ultimate, so the value is moderate rather than game-ending; your W healing is the real equalizer here.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 are still Riven's strongest window: her Broken Wings chain with Ki Burst in the middle and Valor shielding your burst means every extended trade has her dealing physical damage while your heal tries to compensate. The trade pattern you want is: bait Valor first by poking with Chain Lash, then once that shield-dash is on its 6-10s cooldown, chain in with Abduct and immediately fire Kingslayer for the missing-health damage and heal, weaving Petricite autos between casts. Do not let her Valor out cleanly before Kingslayer lands — if she shields the Q and dashes away, you healed nothing. At level 6 the lane does not reset: Blade of the Exile grants attack damage and range, which your AP build cannot spend, so your healing remains the real equalizer.

notes: The Abduct stun correction is Medium confidence and matches the mirror's position: Riot's E text describes a dash plus a recast chain pull, and the derived kit carries no hardCC flag, but Riot's text is not proof of absence. This one claim underpins the trade plan in five sylas__riven fields and appears champion-wide, so a single League Wiki check on Abduct would settle it for every sylas matchup at once — worth doing before this batch is applied.
